rows.derivation: SR1 admits only local-storage and working-storage: a CONSTANT RECORD in LINKAGE and in a FILE SECTION record must be rejected (COBOLNET1549, the SR1 arm); the positive admits both allowed sections and shows their VALUEs (WS=WSOK, LS=LSOK).
citations: cite.py --check 13.18.15.3 "The CONSTANT RECORD clause may be specified only in the local-storage or working-storage sections" -> OK §13.18.15.3 1)
rows.notes: Negatives reject at 2002/2014/2023 with the SR1 message. Not reject-at 85: CONSTANT RECORD itself is a 2002 construct (0900 there), so the SR1 code would not appear.

rows.derivation: CG contains only CI, which contains only CT OCCURS 0 TO 5 DEPENDING ON NN with NN=0. That makes CG a zero-length group by §8.5.4 items 2 and 1 (minimum length 0, runtime length 0). CONTROL IS CG breaks GR6, so the program must be rejected.
citations: cite.py --check 13.18.16.4 "Data-name-1 shall not reference a zero-length group item" -> OK §13.18.16.4 6)
cite.py --check 8.5.4 "A zero-length item is a data item or a literal whose minimum length is zero and whose length at runtime is zero" -> OK §8.5.4
cite.py --check 8.5.4 "A group data item containing only a subordinate zero-length item" -> OK §8.5.4 2)
cite.py --check 8.5.4 "A group data item containing only an occurs-depending table in which the number of occurrences is zero" -> OK §8.5.4 1)
cite.py --check 13.18.38.3 "Integer-1 shall be greater than or equal to zero and integer-2 shall be greater than integer-1" -> OK §13.18.38.3 16)
cite.py --check 13.18.16.3 "The entry specified by data-name-1 shall not have an occurs-depending table subordinate to it" -> OK §13.18.16.3 5)
rows.notes: The diagnostic is COBOLNET1699, which the compiler reports as the §13.18.16.3 SR5 arm. GR6 has no code of its own. Any zero-length group you can know about at compile time also has an ODO table (SR5) or a variable-length member (SR7) under it, so 1699 is the only rejection possible. The director should decide whether an SR5-worded diagnostic is acceptable as the GR6 witness. This group differs from pb177-control-occurs-depending: that group has minimum length 3 and is not zero-length, while this one is zero-length and is reached through a nested group (§8.5.4 item 2). §8.5.4 item 5 (a record whose length is zero at runtime) cannot be observed, as the adjudicator noted.

rows.derivation: Both sentences are about the source LISTING. COBOL.NET produces no listing (docs/CONFORMANCE.md line ~514: '>>LISTING / >>PAGE ... no source listing is produced'), so nothing can be observed through the runner's stdout comparison.

rows.derivation: 85: spaces may be added only BETWEEN text-words, so the literals "A  B.C" and "X,Y;" (each one text-word) copy verbatim; the replacement pseudo-text "P  Q" keeps both inner spaces; and the renamed NEW-A is one word (NEW-A(3:2) = ' B'). 2002: a partial-word match rewrites INSIDE one text-word, so LEADING PFX- BY NEW- gives the single word NEW-NAME, TRAILING -SFX BY -TAG gives CODE-TAG, and LEADING DEL- BY ==== gives ITEM (N=AAA T=BBB D=CCC). Any added space would stop the program compiling.
citations: cite.py --check 7.2.3.4 "The resultant text after replacement shall be in logical free-form reference format" -> OK §7.2.3.4 11)
cite.py --check 7.2.3.4 "Each occurrence of a separator comma, semicolon, or space in pseudo-text-1 or in the library text is considered to be a single space" -> OK §7.2.3.4 9) a) [text is 9) c) 1.]
cite.py --check 7.2.3.4 "When a match occurs between pseudo-text-1 and the library text, the corresponding pseudo-text-2" -> OK §7.2.3.4 9) a) [text is 9) f)]

cite.py --check 7.2.3.4 "When a match occurs between partial-word-1 and the library text-word, the library text-word is placed into the resultant text with the matched characters either replaced by partial-word-2 or deleted" -> OK §7.2.3.4 9) a) [text is 9) f)]
rows.notes: Both goldens also pass at 2023. The .cpy copybooks must be registered or copied next to their .cob (corpus precedent: 2023/*.cpy). cite.py labels the sub-items of GR9 as '9) a)', the same labelling quirk as the PB308 family. The partial-word golden sits in 2002 because LEADING/TRAILING partial words are a 2002 feature. OBSERVATION, not filed: the compiler also ACCEPTS COPY ... REPLACING LEADING at --std 85, and constructs.json has no edition gate for it. If partial words are really post-85, that is under-rejection at 85. I could not verify this without the 1985 text, so no defect entry was filed.

rows.derivation: Uniform size b (documented as 2, DOC-A.1-213). BYTE-LENGTH of PIC N items holding U+0041, U+20AC and U+65E5 is 02 for each (A=02 E=02 J=02). The literals N"A" and N"€" are 02 each. BYTE-LENGTH(N-A)=BYTE-LENGTH(N-J) prints SAME.

rows.derivation: N PIC 9(3) is numeric (8.5.2.12 1). B PIC 9(3) BLANK WHEN ZERO is numeric-edited (8.5.2.13 2). INITIALIZE REPLACING picks receivers by category (14.9.20.4 GR2, 5c2). REPLACING NUMERIC BY 7 changes only N (1 N=007 B=042). REPLACING NUMERIC-EDITED BY 5 changes only B (2 N=007 B=005). ADD 1 TO N gives 3 N=008. Negative: COMPUTE R = B + 1 is rejected because 8.8.1.1 admits only identifiers of numeric data items (COBOLNET0844, whose message names category numeric-edited).

rows.derivation: I1 and I2 get USAGE INDEX implicitly from G USAGE INDEX (13.18.60.4 GR1). As index data items (GR10), they hold occurrence numbers through SET. Occurrence 4 round-trips (1 TE=D) and occurrence 1 round-trips (2 TE=A). SET I2 TO I1 makes I1 = I2 true (3 EQ), and I2 then yields occurrence 4 (4 TE=D). Explicit IX round-trips occurrence 2 (5 TE=B). Only round-trips and equality are asserted, because the representation belongs to the implementor. Negative: MOVE 5 TO I1 breaks 13.18.60.3 SR10 (COBOLNET0809, a MOVE operand of class index).

rows.derivation: 4a intermediate fixed before any store: ADD X TO X Y gives 10/06, COMPUTE X Y = X+1 gives 06/06, MULTIPLY X BY X Y gives 25/10. 4b left-to-right with receivers identified on access: ADD 1 TO I T(I) gives I=2 T=010, and COMPUTE I T(I) = 2 gives T=020. 4a senders identified at the start: ADD T(I) TO I T(I) gives I=3 T=202. 4b size error on one receiver: ADD 5 TO S1 S2 leaves S1=7 and sets S2=12, with SE shown after the stores. 4a size error in the initial evaluation: 1/0 leaves V=3 W=4.
